title: Image-Level Regression for Uncertainty-Aware Retinal Image Segmentation (SAUNA)
note: Variant of soft_band_jml: thickness-normalised soft crack target (width differs by source, 1.5 to 3.25 px) with generalised JML instead of the plain Gaussian band. Run only if soft_band_jml passes its screen against the jml_hard control. Code exists (Oulu-IMEDS/SAUNA). Separate sigmoid regression head is not part of the variant.

title: TRACE: Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement for Thin-Structure Segmentation
note: Not covered: scnp_cedice penalises neighbour pixels, cc_dicece_crack reweights components, clce_crack and Skeleton Recall use a fixed label skeleton. TRACE supervises the bottleneck pixel of the easiest reconnection under the current prediction, with candidate support widened by 1 px for jitter. R: DeepCrack Dice 82.78 to 85.20, beta error 6.16 to 3.69, beats Skeleton Recall and clDice there. No code, about 150 lines in house. Target: crack component recall (0.798), the weakest crack number besides labelling noise.

title: Dice Semimetric Losses: Optimizing the Dice Score with Soft Labels
note: Dice-side counterpart of JML. Variant of soft_band_jml: swap the JML term for the Dice semimetric on the same soft band. Run only if soft_band_jml passes. On hard labels it equals the house Dice (BRIEF 5 Dice rows), so it is soft-label only. Code exists (JDTLosses).

title: Widest-Path Reachability Fields for Connectivity-Preserving Slender Structure Segmentation
note: Alternative solver for the same goal as TRACE (P117), and the scout says pick one. TRACE has numbers on a crack set and beats named baselines, this has abstract-level evidence only. No code. Reopen if trace_crack passes and a second connectivity loss is wanted for the benchmark.

title: The Lovasz-Softmax Loss: A Tractable Surrogate for the Optimization of the Intersection-Over-Union Measure in Neural Networks
note: Benchmark loss row (smp ships it). T2 spec section 0.4: on hard labels it rewards the same pooled IoU as the house Dice; JML paper App. E finds Lovasz equal to JML with hard labels (75.53 vs 75.55). Not run as a candidate; also covered as jml_hard control.

title: Improving Semantic Segmentation via Video Propagation and Label Relaxation
note: Same hypothesis as soft_band_jml (labels jitter by about 1 px, so a prediction 1 px off should not be punished), done as a loss on hard labels. Not VOID: offset-tolerant CE (BRIEF 5 Loss row) was a min over shifts, this is a summed-probability window. Parked because soft_band_jml tests the jitter hypothesis first; if it passes, run this as a hard-target comparator (about 2 h build).

title: Unified Focal loss: Generalising Dice and cross entropy-based losses to handle class imbalanced medical image segmentation
note: Benchmark loss row (focal and Tversky family, BRIEF 5 lists it as untested). T2 spec 0.4: Tversky tied CEDice on Crack500 and TopoMortar in the SCNP tables; recall-favouring asymmetry is an operating-point shift that the matched operating point read would cancel.

title: Boundary-Local Soft Supervision for Reliable Calibration in Defect Segmentation
note: Variant of soft_band_jml: local-mean soft targets inside a 2 px band, also applied to inactive. Gain claimed is calibration, not IoU, so run only if soft_band_jml passes, and read ECE and the cross-fitted bias point. No code.

title: Skeleton Recall Loss for Connectivity Conserving and Resource Efficient Segmentation of Thin Tubular Structures
note: Already run (BRIEF 5 Loss row: w 1.0 widened, w 0.1 narrow E1 pass). Kept as benchmark baseline loss. Open item only: score the trained w 0.1 fresh-seed replication and add the width ratio W. Not VOID because the replication is unscored.

title: How Do Label Errors Affect Thin Crack Detection by DNNs
note: Benchmark design input: score cracks as 1 px curves (relF1 on skeletons) and add a label-error robustness column (synthetic jitter and dropped segments). Findings: under-annotation hurts more than over-annotation. Not a model arm.

title: SoftSeg: Advantages of soft versus binary training for image segmentation
note: Soft-target regression on a blurred crack map: same mechanism as SAUNA (P031), which is thin-structure specific and has stronger evidence, and the soft band in soft_band_jml. Evidence here is brain MRI. Reopen only if the SAUNA variant passes and a plain regression head is wanted.

title: Topologically faithful image segmentation via induced matching of persistence barcodes (Betti matching)
note: Persistent homology loss; same mechanism as P481 (fast C++ version of the same method), so only one would be run. TopoMortar (R) shows PH losses cost Dice on cracks (TopoLoss CrackTree 0.52) and TRACE beats Betti matching on DeepCrack. trace_crack and cc_dicece_crack test component recall first. Reopen if both fail to move component recall.

title: Topograph: An efficient Graph-Based Framework for Strictly Topology Preserving Image Segmentation
note: Component-graph topology loss, same goal as trace_crack and cc_dicece_crack, abstract-level evidence only, no crack result. Its strict homotopy metric is a possible benchmark topology score, to be considered when the benchmark metric list is fixed. Reopen as a loss only if the topology losses show an effect.

title: RankSEG-RMA: An Efficient Segmentation Algorithm via Reciprocal Moment Approximation
note: Decoding rule, not a training change. Per-image Dice and IoU optimisation versus our pooled IoU; val bias at 100% labels gave about 0 (BRIEF 5 Inference row), so a gain on test is expected to be small. Use as a decoding row for per-cell benchmark metrics, dumps already allow it on CPU.

title: Structure-Aware Image Segmentation with Homotopy Warping
note: No code, CPU warping cost over 20k steps unprofiled. Evidence (R, TopoMortar): CrackTree Dice 0.77 vs 0.78 CEDice, no gain in supervised training. Weaker than trace_crack, which targets the same critical pixels with a cheaper local search.

title: Efficient Betti Matching Enables Topology-Aware 3D Segmentation via Persistent Homology
note: Fast implementation of the same method as P413. If a PH loss is ever run, use this one (code exists). Parked for the same reasons as P413: PH cost, TRACE tables show it weaker than TRACE on DeepCrack, trace_crack is tested first.

title: Centerline Boundary Dice Loss for Vascular Segmentation (cbDice)
note: On crack (radius about 1 px) it is close to soft clDice, which failed here (BRIEF 5 Loss row), and clce_crack tests the centerline mechanism. Only the multi-class width balance is untested and has no evidence on EL. R: no topology gain over CEDice on CrackTree in TopoMortar. Reopen if inactive and ribbons need width-balanced loss.

title: Optimization for Medical Image Segmentation: Theory and Practice When Evaluating With Dice Score or Jaccard Index
note: Theory paper. Defines the benchmark loss axis (CE, CE+Dice, CE+JML, Lovasz under one protocol) and the warning that Tversky trades IoU for recall. No arm.

title: TOPO-Loss for continuity-preserving crack detection using deep learning
note: Crack-domain continuity loss with code, but R (TopoMortar) finds it unstable (CREMI Dice 0.63 +- 0.22) and over-segmenting out of distribution; evidence is masonry crack sets only. trace_crack has stronger evidence for the same continuity goal. Reopen if trace_crack passes and a second continuity loss is wanted.
